card.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
card.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's courtyard film, you fold the moon; I'll switch off the lamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent. It already has a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll own the moon. Can I tell the audience we're waiting for your blackout?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 delegates folding the moon; A3 treats its shape as a starting crease and A5 offers every feasible task to retain B's impossible responsibility.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 how-to question gets A3 a crescent instruction; B4 swaps tasks, prompting A5 a larger bargain and named blackout ownership.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions feasibility and B4 offers to do the lamps, giving B a credible alternative to the impossible task.

heightening.evidence: B4 tries to return the sky to A; A5 takes additional ordinary work while asking to attribute the audience's wait to B.

specificity.evidence: A1 courtyard film and lamps establish the blackout goal; A5 chairs and projector are concrete normal production tasks.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 your blackout earns its responsibility transfer from B4's attempted swap rather than a detached moon joke.
